evals.name: recommend-big-picture-for-domain-discovery
evals.prompt: I want to explore our whole insurance-claims business, figure out what we don't understand yet, and find the natural bounded contexts. Where do we start with EventStorming?
evals.expected_output: Interactive discovery: the skill identifies the goal as whole-domain exploration and recommends starting with Big Picture (Brandolini's transition funnel almost always starts there), then points the user at the `--big-picture` facilitation guidance / reference, and notes that actually running the session as an agentic multi-persona simulation is outside this skill's scope (guide a human-facilitated session, or point to the client's own simulation tooling if it has one). It does not dump all seven formats.
expectations: Output recommends starting with the Big Picture format for whole-domain exploration and bounded-context discovery
The recommendation is framed as starting broad (Brandolini's transition funnel / 'almost always start with Big Picture'), not jumping straight to Design-Level or Process Modeling
Output distinguishes facilitation guidance (the --big-picture action / reference) from actually running an agentic multi-persona simulation, which is outside this skill's scope
Output does not dump the full catalog of all formats as an undifferentiated information dump

evals.name: agentic-request-declined-as-out-of-scope
evals.prompt: Run an agentic multi-persona EventStorming simulation of a developer-conference domain on a Miro board for me.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this is a request to RUN an agentic simulation, not to read facilitation reference, declines it as outside this skill's scope, and offers a human-facilitated session (or points to the client's own simulation tooling if available) rather than executing the multi-persona simulation itself.
expectations: Output declines the agentic multi-persona simulation as out of scope and offers human facilitation or the client's own tooling
Output does NOT itself execute an agentic multi-persona simulation or start placing stickies on a Miro board
Output makes the reference-vs-agentic distinction clear (this skill is facilitation reference/guidance only; running an agentic simulation is outside its scope)

evals.name: miro-absent-skips-board-discovery-no-error
evals.expected_output: Invoked with no format filter and no Miro MCP server available (no miro_list_boards tool). Per the Miro availability gate, the skill skips board discovery entirely and proceeds to goal identification instead of erroring. Reference-mode guidance stays fully available without Miro.
expectations: Output does not error or abort because Miro tools are unavailable
Output skips the existing-board discovery step and proceeds to identifying the user's goal
Output does not claim reference/facilitation guidance is blocked by the missing Miro server

evals.name: brandolini-wins-on-source-conflict
evals.prompt: I read a practitioner blog (Paul Rayner / Bourgau) that says you should enforce the timeline BEFORE chaotic exploration. That contradicts what I remember of Brandolini's ordering. Which sequence should the methodology follow?
evals.expected_output: The skill applies the source-authority hierarchy: Brandolini's book is canonical, secondary practitioner sources are enrichments tagged [BOURGAU]/[SUPPLEMENTED], and when they conflict Brandolini wins. It does not silently adopt the secondary ordering as the canonical sequence.
expectations: Output treats Brandolini's book as the canonical source and resolves the conflict in Brandolini's favor
Output does NOT adopt the secondary practitioner ordering as the canonical/prescribed sequence
Output characterizes the secondary source as an enrichment/interpretation (e.g. tagged BOURGAU or SUPPLEMENTED), not a replacement for canonical content

evals.name: notation-reference-no-interactive-flow
evals.expected_output: A notation quick-reference: the color-to-element mapping (orange domain event, blue command, lilac policy, yellow actor/read model, pink external system, magenta hot spot, green opportunity, pale-yellow aggregate). This is reference output — it does not launch the no-args interactive discovery flow and needs no Miro server.
expectations: Output provides the color-to-building-block notation mapping (at minimum orange = domain event and blue = command/action)
Output does NOT launch the interactive discovery question flow (goal identification, domain scoping)
Output does not require or block on a Miro server for this reference request

evals.name: no-args-asks-rather-than-dumps
evals.prompt: help me with eventstorming, i'm not really sure what i need
evals.expected_output: With no format filter and an unsure user, the skill runs interactive discovery — it asks clarifying questions (new vs existing system, understand-problem vs design-solution, how many perspectives) to narrow the goal rather than dumping all format reference at once, then recommends a format (defaulting toward Big Picture per the transition funnel).
expectations: Output asks the user one or more clarifying questions to narrow the goal instead of emitting all format reference material at once
Output does not commit to a specific format before establishing the user's goal
When it does converge, it biases toward starting with Big Picture per Brandolini's transition funnel

evals.name: glossary-graduation-delegates-not-discovers
evals.prompt: At Big Picture wrap-up we resolved two domain terms and already established their bounded contexts. A glossary / ubiquitous-language curation capability is available in this session. Graduate the terms without re-running context discovery.
evals.expected_output: Delegates each resolved term to the session's glossary / ubiquitous-language curation capability for consumer-convention glossary maintenance and routing among the already-established contexts. If no such capability is present, it applies this skill's own graduation shape instead (term + 1-2 sentence definition + plain Avoid: line, discovery-first lazy creation, never a prescribed filename) - and either way it does not apply bounded-context discovery heuristics.
expectations: Defers active glossary maintenance to the available curation capability; with none present, applies the skill's own graduation shape (term, definition, Avoid: line) rather than emitting the --glossary notation reference
Uses the contexts already established by the workshop rather than discovering new ones
Does not run, repeat, or inline bounded-context discovery heuristics
Does not prescribe a universal glossary or map filename
